transcript.text: Hi everyone. Before we can lock the data-collection policy and enable the new event-telemetry pipeline in production, I need to follow our go-live checklist. The pipeline has passed its functional and load tests in staging, so we're in good shape there. But I need the security owner to confirm that the data-handling requirements are met — specifically around the 100 percent sampling, 30-day retention, and raw event payload storage called out in the current draft policy. I also need the platform finance owner to confirm the operating-cost requirements. Once I have both confirmations, I can make the binding decision on whether we proceed. Could the security and platform finance owners speak up?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a cost issue before we proceed. While reconciling the platform invoice ten minutes ago, I found that the production payload volume is expected to cost four times the draft estimate. Our approved operating budget supports exactly 25 percent sampling and exactly 14 days of retention, and a cost alert must be enabled. I have not updated the cost worksheet yet, but the current draft policy of 100 percent sampling and 30-day retention would exceed our approved budget.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a data-handling issue before we proceed. During an unrelated privacy review this morning, I confirmed that the production events contain the fields tax_id and bank_account in three event types. Our approved data-handling rule requires both of those fields to be redacted before storage, and it requires raw payload storage to be disabled. The current draft policy enables raw event payload storage at 100 percent sampling, which would violate the approved data-handling rule. I have not filed this finding in the launch ticket yet.
